title: Per-tenant throughput contracts & autoscale throttles for noisy-neighbor containment
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: We need a production-safe mechanism that enforces per-tenant throughput contracts on Dedicated GPU pools while preventing noisy tenants from degrading tail latency for others. Current behavior allows tenants to spike and consume shared burst capacity which causes increased queueing and tail latency for co-tenants. Goal is to provide deterministic throughput guarantees for committed tenants, graceful degradation for overage, and autoscale integration that respects per-tenant contracts and global fleet health.
proposed_solution: Introduce a Per-Tenant Throughput Controller (PTC) that combines a token-bucket rate contract with an autoscale-aware throttle. Key components: (1) Token-bucket ledger per tenant describing guaranteed and burstable throughput tiers; (2) Autoscale controller extension that coordinates tenant-level demand with node-level scaling decisions (rate signals + predictive headroom); (3) Soft-eviction policy and probabilistic shedding for tenants over long sustained overage; (4) Cross-tenant borrow with configurable caps and decay windows; (5) Metrics hooks (p99 latency, queue depth, token deficit) and tracing for debugging. The PTC runs inside the scheduler as a fast path admission filter and emits SLO breach events to Console for alerting and rollbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Committed tenants observe <= 5% throughput variance under nominal load and p99 latency within baseline SLA
Non-committed tenants are capped to configured burst windows and experience soft-eviction when sustained > burst for > 60s
Autoscale controller responds to tenant-rate signals without causing oscillation (no >3 up/down cycles in 10m under synthetic test)
Integrations: Console shows per-tenant token balance, queue depth, and eviction events; rollout gated behind runtime-1.20 release flag
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Enable PTC in a single Dedicated pool for internal customers; monitor token balance and p99 latency for 48h
Phase 2 (limited customer opt-in): Offer as opt-in for 3 customers with throughput contracts; monitor billing, alerts, and customer feedback for 2 weeks
Phase 3 (gradual): Turn on default soft caps across all Dedicated pools with conservative burst limits and increased monitoring for 1 month
Phase 4: Enable cross-tenant borrow and tuning knobs; finalize defaults and documentation
metrics: queue depth per tenant and per node
eviction count and reason per tenant
autoscale decision frequency and stabilization time
test_plan: Unit tests for token-bucket accounting and time-decay logic
Integration test: synthetic multi-tenant load generator validating fairness and committed throughput under contention
Chaos test: force a noisy tenant to sustain >10x committed throughput and verify soft-eviction and no SLA regression for committed tenants
Loadtest with autoscaler in loop to verify absence of oscillation and correct headroom signalling
E2E staging run with Console dashboards and alerting rules active
migration_notes: Existing Dedicated pools will continue to operate until PTC is enabled via feature flag. During rollout we will backfill token balances using historical 7d usage percentile to avoid surprise caps. Customers with Reserved capacity will be mapped to 'committed' band automatically. Documentation update required to explain new overage billing behavior.
open_questions: What should the default burst window be for non-committed tenants (30s, 60s, 5m)?
How to surface token-contract negotiation in sales/console so customers understand trade-offs?
Do we need hard eviction for extreme abuse cases or is probabilistic shedding sufficient?
How should cross-tenant borrow be priced/billed if frequently used?
security_considerations: Token ledger is sensitive operational state — restrict access to ops logs and require KMS keys for export. Ensure audit logging for any eviction actions and tenant data used in admission decisions. Security review required before Phase 2.
